name: studio
description: The index, the spec pages, the writing, and the links, served as static files from GitHub Pages. Every route is written out at build time, so a crawler gets a real document rather than an empty shell.

The catalog is one JSON file. Adding a part writes its index card, its spec page, its prerendered path, and its metadata — no second edit. The design rules live in a shared stylelint config, so a banned border-radius fails the build rather than shipping.

name: watchthediff
tagline: Watches the watchers. Tracks those who track you.
description: Daily, automated diffs of privacy policies and terms from the largest AI companies. Every material change is detected, classified, scored, and dated — so you can see exactly how AI data-use language shifts over time.

name: knurl-icons
tagline: Draws 24×24 stroke icons that pass as Lucide.
description: A browser editor for 24×24 stroke icons that conform to the Lucide standard. Draw on the grid, watch conformance score in real time, and export SVG a serializer will round-trip.

The serializer is gated against 1847 real upstream Lucide icons: every one is a byte-level fixed point under re-serialization, and 1839 of them rasterize pixel-identically to upstream at 24, 96 and 384px. The remaining eight are an allowlist, each with a written reason.

name: delia
tagline: A 128×64 LED matrix on a Raspberry Pi, run from a phone.
description: A 128×64 RGB HUB75 panel driven by a Pi 3 A+. A long-lived root daemon owns the panel and renders declarative scene documents; an unprivileged Flask API validates them and forwards them over a Unix socket, and the daemon validates them again — it is the trust boundary.

The phone UI is a React and TypeScript SPA, built on a laptop rather than the Pi. The engine runs in CI against a mock backend, so the renderer is tested without any hardware attached. The panel lives on the home network; the source is public.
